Conservation Tip: A Greener Holiday Starts at Home

Looking for simple ways to keep the holidays festive and environmentally friendly? Start by swapping incandescent lights for LEDs—according to the U.S. Department of Energy, they use at least 75 percent less energy and last up to 25 times longer. Bring nature indoors with pinecones, fresh greenery, dried herbs, cinnamon sticks or dried orange slices for décor that looks great and leaves a light footprint.

To cut down on waste, “shop your home” before buying anything new, choose durable decorations that last for years and recycle cardboard boxes from online shopping. Skip wrapping paper with foil or glitter (it isn’t recyclable), and consider regifting or donating items you already have. For a low-waste option, homemade treats always make thoughtful gifts. 

Small choices add up—here’s to a greener holiday season!

Feel Good All Season Long

Just like the bears, it’s easy to hibernate at home during the cold winter months. Don’t let the cold weather stall your fitness goals! 

Looking for the perfect snack for holiday movie night? Try our Food and Nutrition Office’s chili popcorn—a savory crowd-pleaser.

If you want to stay active through the season, check out our Holiday Fitness Videos playlist on YouTube. Quick workouts, family-friendly routines and festive movement breaks make it easy to keep your energy up.

From tasty recipes to fun fitness ideas, we’re here to help you enjoy a balanced holiday season!

Create Something Joyful This Winter

Get ready to start your new year off on a creative note! 

Registration for winter classes through the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center opens on Dec. 13 at 8:30 a.m. While the Tyson Cultural Arts Center undergoes exciting renovations, Session One classes will take place at the Fran Ryan Center, Columbus Performing Arts Center and Whetstone Community Center.

Registration for winter classes at the Fran Ryan Center opens on Dec. 27 at 9 a.m.

There’s plenty to explore—find something new to inspire you this season!

Holiday Joy In Every Neighborhood

The holiday season is in full swing, and our community centers are ready to celebrate with you. Many locations are hosting free holiday meals, offering warm clothing and sharing gifts for kids. Events run through Dec. 19—check with your local community center for details.

These celebrations are supported in part by the Adopt a Center program. A big thank-you to our presenting sponsor, Columbus City Council, our Angel Partner, Columbia Gas, and many other central Ohio organizations, businesses and individuals helping spread joy across our neighborhoods! Want to get involved, and help spread joy this holiday season? There is still time to donate to the Adopt a Center program!

Know someone who loves spending time on the course? Make their season bright with golf gift cards to the department’s six municipal golf courses. A Message from the Director: Grateful For You

Dear CRPD Team, 

As we enter into the holiday season, this year is very unique. As a country, state and community, we have faced challenges. It is a time for us to think of loved ones that are no longer with us and spread love with ones that are here.

We will always be thankful for the joy that each of you share every day. We have the opportunity to change the lives of people we work beside, people throughout our community and others we don’t know. This happens as we continue to Lift Each Other up with the kindness of words and acts of love.

My gratitude is for the dedication that you show daily, but also because you all show up every day to make a difference. As we continue to Build Strong Connections, let’s share a smile, and be thankful for each other.

Happy Thanksgiving!

Sincerely,

Bernita

A December Must-See: The Topiary Garden

If you haven’t visited the Topiary Garden at Deaf School Park, this is the perfect time to go! Tucked behind the Columbus Metropolitan Library’s Main Library, the garden recreates Georges Seurat’s iconic painting, A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of LaGrande Jatte, using more than 50 sculpted topiaries shaped by Columbus artist James T. Mason and his wife, Elaine. With Seurat’s birthday on Dec. 2, it’s a great moment to explore this living tribute—complete with strolling couples, parasols and even a small dog. Don’t miss the “As He Saw It” viewpoint that aligns with Seurat’s original perspective. And while the original painting hangs in the Art Institute of Chicago, Columbus’ own topiary masterpiece offers an unforgettable way to experience it close to home.

Warm Up Your Winter: Sign Up for Adult Sports

Ready to get active this winter? Adult volleyball and basketball registration opens Dec. 5 at 10 a.m. and closes Dec. 19. Whether you’re looking to stay competitive, meet new people or simply have fun, our leagues offer something for everyone.

Sign up today!

Make some holiday ornaments, paint a holiday scene or learn the basics of embroidery or model railroading. There’s something for every interest and schedule!

Looking for festive plans the weekend of Dec. 5? The Golden Hobby Shop at the Fran Ryan Center has you covered! Join us on Friday, Dec. 5, from 4-8 p.m. for our Sip & Shop—$1 gets you in the door with a beverage in hand as you browse new handmade inventory perfect for holiday gifting.

Come back on Saturday, Dec. 6, from 11 a.m.-2 p.m. for Holiday Hoopla, a free, family-friendly celebration where you can sip hot chocolate, and create your own gifts and decorations. RSVP is appreciated (614-724-2550 or FRC@columbus.gov) but not required.

Kick off the holiday season with a touch of creativity!

Columbus Recreation and Parks Earns Five OPRA Awards — Thanks to You

Columbus Recreation and Parks Department has been recognized with five Ohio Parks and Recreation Association Awards of Excellence—more than any other agency this year. And while the awards are exciting, they’re really a testament to something bigger: the power of residents who show up, participate and believe in what parks can do for a community. The winning entries were:

  • Franklinton Parks and Souder Avenue Pedestrian Bridge Projects: First place in Capital Improvement Projects: $3-$10 Million
  • Fran Ryan Center: Second place in Capital Improvement Projects: $10 Million and Up
  • CBUS Soul® Fest: Second Place in Historical and Cultural Arts
  • Growing the Game: Equity and Opportunity Through Golf: Third Place in Recreational Programs
  • Millard D. Morgan, I, Driving Park Community Center: Youth Sports Coach of the Year

From major capital projects to cultural festivals to programs that open doors for youth, these honors reflect what happens when Columbus works together. 

Thank you to every resident who visits our parks, joins our programs, volunteers time or supports neighborhood improvements. Your involvement makes this recognition possible, and makes our community stronger!

Kilbourne Run Sports Park Moves Into the Next Phase

Kilbourne Run Sports Park is taking shape as one of Columbus’ premier sports destinations. The first phase wrapped in October with all six full-sized turf fields installed, and two have already hosted tournament play in a successful trial run! Rental permits for 2026 are now open.

There’s more to come! Construction on the championship stadium is underway. The four surrounding grass fields on the west side of the park have been seeded and will be available for rental in fall 2026. Key amenities are also coming together. Parking lots, walking paths and both new playgrounds are now installed. The roundabout at Westerville Road and the entry drive to the park are anticipated to open by the end of December.

Kilbourne Run is more than a project—it’s a major investment in community, sports access and economic impact. More progress is on the way!

A Message to All Staff: ACTIVENet Update is Approaching Soon

Dear CRPD Team, 

You probably heard this mentioned in the last quarterly leadership staff meeting, but we are upgrading our department’s ACTIVENet system on Tuesday, Dec. 9. ACTIVENet is where residents sign up to register for classes and camps and rent event venues. While residents won’t see many changes to how they use ACTIVENet, the upgrade will improve the department’s processes and make it easier to implement upgrades in the future. The new ACTIVENet will not be available until Dec. 9.

Essentially, If residents have not used ACTIVENet in 2025, they will need to create a new account when they log in. All users will need to update their passwords for the new ACTIVENet. They can do this when they log into ACTIVENet for the first time after the change. 

You can learn more about the ACTIVENet system update. This webpage has next steps and FAQs. Please read through this information so you’re prepared to answer questions from residents.

Please reach out to Tony Brodie (ALBrodie@columbus.gov) or Stan Bulejski (SRBulejski@columbus.gov) if you have any questions.

Conservation Tip: Spotted Lanternflies are in Ohio

The spotted lanternfly, an invasive insect, has been confirmed in Ohio. Early concerns suggested they might be as destructive as the emerald ash borer, but research from Penn State shows that spotted lanternflies pose very little risk to native trees. Because the pest is already established in our region and evidence suggests there won't be long-term impacts to public trees, the City’s Forestry team is not treating for spotted lanternfly. 

The Ohio Department of Agriculture recommends removing grapevines and tree-of-heaven from your property if you are worried about the pest, since it primarily threatens vineyards and orchards.

Residents can still help slow the spread. If you see a spotted lanternfly, you can stomp adults to kill them, and scrape or destroy egg masses when you find them. You can learn more tips on controlling spotted lanternflies.

Dear CRPD Team, 

Veterans Day is about honoring those who have served. It’s also about honoring those who haven’t served – advocates, family members and friends.

This year, it’s more important than ever to reflect on that. Our country is facing real challenges, and many in our community are struggling. So how do we honor those who have served us?

We serve others.

Whether it’s helping a veteran, a family member or a neighbor, that is the spirit of public service. And you bring it to life. Every day, you show what service looks like. Right now, many of you are helping with the City’s SNAP Support program that is making food accessible to our community in a critical time of need. That is service in action.

I appreciate you for serving the City of Columbus each day. Your work matters, and I appreciate you!

Sincerely, 

~Bernita

Bernita A. Reese, M.S., CPRP
Director, Columbus Recreation and Parks Department

It’s deer season, and they’re doing what deer do best—running around like they own the place! 

According to the Ohio State Highway Patrol, deer-related crashes spike after daylight saving time ends, especially around sunrise and sunset. If you see a deer on the road, brake—don’t swerve. They travel in groups, so if one appears, assume it brought friends.

Conservation Tip: Leave the Leaves In Your Yard This Fall

As the leaves start to fall, skip the bags, and let nature do the work. According to the National Wildlife Federation, Americans throw away more than 35 million tons of yard waste each year. Leaves provide vital habitat for butterflies, fireflies, birds, small mammals and more—and they help return nutrients to the soil.

Spread a light layer over your yard, or place leaves in garden beds and under trees. It’s an easy way to support wildlife and your landscape.

Learn more tips from the National Wildlife Federation.

Supporting Families with Food Access Resources

Columbus Recreation and Parks is committed to our community—and especially to our neighbors whose lives are being impacted by the federal government shutdown. If you or someone you know needs support with food access, we’re here to help.

Fresh Produce: Every Thursday and Friday, stop by our Mobile Produce Markets at select community centers through Nov. 21 to pick up fresh produce at no cost. No registration or paperwork required.

Free Meals for Students: School-age children can also receive a free meal every weekday from 3:30-5 p.m. at our Afterschool Program sites. All are welcome. Participating community centers include Adams, Barack, Blackburn, Douglas, Driving Park, Far East, Glenwood, Holton, Howard, Linden, Milo Grogan, Sullivant Gardens, Feddersen and Woodward Park community centers.

If you need support, please come. If someone you know could benefit from these resources, feel free to share this message. In times like these, community matters—and Columbus shows up for one another.

A Message to All Staff: Review Benefits Changes and Make Your Elections During Open Enrollment

Dear CRPD Team, 

For the first time, the City of Columbus is moving to one combined Open Enrollment for PPO and HDHP medical plans - no more separate spring PPO enrollment. From Oct. 27–Nov. 30, you can add or remove covered dependents, enroll in coverage, switch plans or waive coverage, and update your 2026 HSA contributions. 

In addition to a new enrollment date, the City is moving to a new medical insurance carrier, Anthem BCBS, so it’s important to thoroughly review your options this year. 

Here’s what you need to do:

  1. Review the 2026 plan information. You can find this in the Open Enrollment home mailer, which was mailed to you (if you don't receive this mailer in the coming days, check to make sure your home address is current in Dayforce). Please note: 2026 premiums are being finalized and will be shared around Nov. 1. You’ll soon be able to access a list of in-network providers. Watch for emails from Employee Benefits and Wellness with this information; we’ll also share information with all staff. 
  2. Make your elections in Dayforce. The type of medical coverage you’re currently enrolled in will determine if you need to take action:
    • If you are currently enrolled in a PPO option and don’t take action, your current coverage will roll over.
    • If you are currently enrolled in an HDHP plan, you must re-elect your HSA contributions each year.
  3. Review beneficiary designations. Even if you don’t make changes, log in to Dayforce to ensure the information is current.

To help you understand these changes, the Employee Benefits and Wellness Office is hosting virtual and in-person information sessions to walk you through your options. The virtual sessions will be recorded and available for playback. Register to save your spot.

Have questions or need help? Check out the FAQs at the end of the Open Enrollment home mailer or call the Employee Benefits and Wellness Office at 614-645-8624 (Monday through Friday). Conservation Tip: Bats, the Nighttime Pest Patrol

When you see bats swooping through the twilight, don’t panic—cheer them on! These flying bug zappers devour thousands of mosquitoes and other pests every night, keeping evenings more comfortable for all of us. Despite their spooky image, most bats are shy, gentle and vital to a healthy ecosystem.

Spotting bats this fall is a great sign that nature’s balance is thriving. However, some local species are even at risk, facing big threats like habitat loss and disease. You can help bats out by skipping or reducing pesticides, hanging a bat house and spreading the word about these hardworking, often misunderstood neighbors of the night.

Get in the Game: 50+ Basketball League Tips Off Soon

Ready to show you’ve still got it? Lace up for the 2025-2026 50+ basketball league! Whether you’ve got a full team or just your game face, there’s a spot for you. Individual players can hit the open gyms to practice (Oct. 12, 19 and 26 from 1-3 p.m. at Barack Community Center), and join a team before the season begins.

Registration runs Oct. 12-27, and the season begins Nov. 2. The 10-week season begins Nov. 2 and includes playoffs for qualifying teams

Bring your completed registration form to an open gym, and get ready for friendly competition, fitness and fun!

Poetry in Motion: Rikki Santer Joins the Fran Ryan Center as Artist in Residence

The Fran Ryan Center is delighted to welcome Rikki Santer as the Winter/Spring 2026 Artist in Residence. From Jan. 5 through May 2, Rikki will share her creative talents through workshops, readings and community engagement.

An award-winning poet, editor and educator, Rikki was named Ohio Poet of the Year in 2023. Her published collections include Clothesline Logic, Fishing for Rabbits and Zebra Lashes.

Watch for more information about her residency!

Harvest Parties: Fall Fun for Everyone

Celebrate the season at our free harvest parties happening at community centers across the city! Enjoy festive games, seasonal treats and good times with neighbors as we welcome autumn together.

Check with your local community center for specific dates and times, and don’t miss out on the fun—fall only comes once a year!

Swing Into National Golf Lover’s Day

Love to golf? Mark your calendar for National Golf Lover’s Day on Saturday, Oct. 4, and book a tee time at one of our six golf courses! With this warm weather, it is the perfect time to enjoy 18 holes at Airport, Champions, Mentel Memorial, Raymond Memorial or Turnberry—or try the 9-hole course at Wilson Road. 

Whether you’re just starting out or a seasoned pro, there’s a course for you! Check out the brand-new short highlight video for Champions Golf Course!

The Spookiest Softball Game in Town

Get ready for a spooky night of fun on the field! A fall staple, Friday Night Frights is back on Friday, Oct. 24. Registration opens Oct. 3 and closes Oct. 17. 

Get your team together, and register early—spots fill up quickly!

New Workshops, Fresh Inspiration

Explore your creativity at the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center. This month’s workshop, Introduction to Comics with Marina Harkness, takes place on Saturday, Oct. 25, from 10 a.m.-4 p.m. ($80). Learn the basics of comics as a visual language, and try your hand at traditional cartooning tools.

Coming in November: Beaded Jewelry 101, Fused Glass Snowflakes, Creative Writing Collage and more.

Get ready to register: create an account, and explore all of the offerings.

Conversations That Connect Columbus: Join The Big Table®

The Big Table® is a community-wide day of conversation designed to spark connection and inspire action. This year, Columbus Recreation and Parks is hosting two conversations—and we want your voice at the table.

Adaptive Programming: Ensuring Access to Recreation: Share your experiences and ideas on how adaptive recreation can better connect residents of all abilities at the Espy Adaptive Sports Complex, 1755 E. Broad St. 

Creating Community Support for Older Americans: Help us explore the resources available for older adults and how the community can strengthen support at the Fran Ryan Center, 865 E. Capital St.

Both conversations happen Tuesday, Oct. 21, from 9-10:30 a.m. Get more information, and register.  

Join us to listen, share and build a more connected Columbus!

Other opportunities include Mobile Produce Markets and Therapeutic Recreation events.
